base.description: The bracket as FS ships DINRAIL2U, assembled, with its rail.

description: 2U 19in adjustable DIN rail bracket, FS DINRAIL2U: two black steel side brackets 360 mm deep whose front ends fold out into ears, joined by a rail panel carrying a 400 mm TS35 DIN rail that slides back along slots in the brackets, so DIN-rail equipment - industrial switches, media converters, power supplies, breakers - can stand in a 19in rack.

gaps.note: no FS document states what the DINRAIL2U or its rail may carry.
FS does not name the rail's profile; TS35 x 7.5 is read off the close-up render.

The tab's 3.9 height on the side views is estimated too: no view dimensions it.

name: dinrail2u

chassis.note: 87.5 x 484 x 360 (HxWxD) over the ears, which is the part. THE EARS ARE BUILT IN: each is the front end of a side bracket folded out flat, one piece with the bracket that forms the frame's side (the datasheet's front and isometric views; renders g1 and g2 of SKU 178163), so under the owner's rule of 2026-10-09 they are part of the face and always drawn, 29.9 each side: the front is the 484 face, and the chassis is the 424.2 between the side brackets, which is what the other five faces and the side brackets in 3D are (as the FHD-1UFMT-N draws its plate). On the 300 dpi front view the outer edges stand 484 apart at 1.37 px/mm and the folds 29.9 in from each.

color.note: black steel and a silver zinc-plated rail, as every render shows.

eia.note: EIA-310 hole positions: the rail holes of each rack unit stand 6.35, 22.225 and 38.1 mm up from its bottom, and the two rails' holes are 465.1 mm apart across the rack. The part is taken as centred in the rack units it fills.

hosting.note: for #935: one TS35 x 7.5 rail, 400 mm long, centred 43.75 mm below the top of the 87.5 mm face, its panel's face 51.2 to 271.2 behind the ears; the width between the side brackets is 421.2; the space available behind the rail runs to the 360 mm depth. FS states no load rating. Recorded in `attrs.physical`.

joint.note: for #971: how the rail panel meets the side brackets. The panel (fs/dinrail2u-panel@2) is the 421.2 between the brackets' inner faces: the datasheet's 400.00 is the rail, and on its top view its plate runs from bracket to bracket, the rail stopping short of each. At each end the panel folds back along the bracket's inner face as a flange, and a tab at its top and bottom lies on the bracket's edge, which is lowered 6.1 between the bracket's ends to take it (the side view, p2; gallery render g4 of SKU 178163). Two M5 screws a side (the quick start guide: "the M5 screws and nuts"; the side view draws two) pass through the bracket's two slots into the flange, which is how the panel slides and is fixed (#950). At the default setback the tab and flange run 161.2 to 197.1 behind the ears and the screws stand at 179.4, the offsets the setback note reads; the screws are common/pan-screw-m5@1, the pan head render g4 shows. The flange is drawn under the side bracket, seen through its slots and window; its depth is taken as the tab's. In the plan views the tab reaches 15.6 in from the bracket's inner face and overhangs its outer face by 8.9 (the top view, 1.116 mm a pixel); the overhang lies outside the plan views, which stop at the brackets, so only the 3D tab on the side views (standing 10.4 off the side, the plate's 1.5 and the overhang) carries it. The screw heads are drawn over the bracket, whole, on its outer face over the slot, as render g4 shows them (the bracket is `under` them), standing the plate's 1.5 off the face. WHAT IS ESTIMATED in this note, the rest being read from the drawings: the tab's 3.9 height on the side views, which no view dimensions (it is drawn to end on the lowered edge, inside the 6.1 step); the flange's depth along the bracket, taken as the tab's, and its height, taken as the whole span between the two tabs; the tab's 15.6 reach and 8.9 overhang, each about 14 and 8 pixels of a raster at 1.1 mm a pixel, so good to a millimetre or so at best; and the 6.1 of the lowered edge, 5.5 pixels of the side view's raster at 1.1 mm a pixel.

rail-setback.note: the rail panel's front face can stand from 51.2 to 271.2 mm behind the ears, and is drawn at 161.2, the middle of that travel; the rail's face stands 7.5 in front of the panel's. The panel slides along the two long slots in each 360 mm side bracket ("the adjustable rails can be easily set back"; QSG: adjust the rail panel's position to suit the device). On the datasheet's side view (p2, an embedded 461 x 212 px raster, about 1.1 mm a pixel, read on a 600 dpi upsampled render at 3.342 px/mm along the 360) the slots run 64.4 to 292 and are about 5.2 wide. The slot's front end is hidden under the screw head drawn at 69.4, so the front stop is taken at that screw rather than at 64.4 + 2.6 = 67.0; a screw's centre travels from 69.4 to 289.4, the front end good to about 1.5 mm. The panel's tab spans 51.2 to 87.1 with its screw at 69.4, so the panel face stands 18.2 in front of the screw. The face travel is the screw travel less that. The gallery renders show it at both ends of that travel: g4 about 85 and g3 about 227 behind the ears, each read along the near side bracket as a fraction of its 360 (a three-quarter render, so to perhaps 10 per cent). With no single photographed position, the middle of the travel is the default. The travel is stated as the `rail-setback` adjustment, whose three stops are the two ends and that middle; the three din-rail-setback attrs restate it.

sheet.note: `shell: sheet`, 1.5: an open frame of bent steel - two side brackets, a rail panel and a rail - which a solid box would hide. In 3D the side brackets are built from the side views, standing their thickness off them. The panel is a well on the front view whose floor is the plate at its setback, black with its cut-outs open, and the rail stands 7.5 off that floor with its face art - flanges, crown, slots - on its front. The six views are elevations.
